d: Explore the wide variety of user interface elements that players can interact with.
h:
You can quickly create high-quality graphical user interfaces with minimal scripting requirements using built-in UI objects. Depending on where you create it, UI renders either on-screen or within a game's 3D world.

On-screen UI

On-screen containers hold UI objects that you want to display on a player's screen, including frames, labels, buttons, and more. All on-screen UI objects and code are stored and changed on the client.

In-game UI

In-game containers such as SurfaceGuis and BillboardGuis hold UI objects that you want to display within your game's 3D world.

UI objects

Most UI elements are GuiObjects, 2D graphical user interface objects that you can parent to containers. The four most common are frames, labels, buttons, and text input objects.

Object Description
[Frame](#/docs/ui/frames) Frames act as containers for other UI objects. When you manipulate frames, you also manipulate the objects they contain.
[Label](#/docs/ui/labels) TextLabel and ImageLabel objects allow you to display customizable text and images.
[Button](#/docs/ui/buttons) TextButton and ImageButton objects allow users to prompt an action.
[Text Input](#/docs/ui/text-input) TextBox objects allow users to input text.

Using the Position, Size, AnchorPoint, and ZIndex properties, you have complete control on how to position, size, and layer GuiObjects. You can also use tweening to transition a GuiObject smoothly from one state to another and provide dynamic visual feedback.

Layout and design

Beyond basic properties for adjusting position and size, Roblox also provides layout structures like list/flex and grid, as well as size modifiers and appearance modifiers.

Universal styling

Universal styling is a Roblox solution to stylesheets, similar to CSS, that lets you declare and globally apply overrides to UI instance properties. This engine‑level support is the foundation for the Style Editor and the end‑to‑end token pipeline.

Interactive frameworks

In addition to the core user interface objects, the following frameworks provide built‑in and customizable interactivity for your games.

Proximity prompts

Proximity prompts are unique built-in UI objects which prompt user interaction to trigger an action when they approach in-game objects such as doors, light switches, and buttons.

UI drag detectors

UI drag detectors facilitate and encourage interaction with 2D user interface elements such as sliders, spinners, and more.

3D drag detectors

3D drag detectors encourage physical interaction with 3D objects in a game, such as opening doors and drawers, sliding a part around, grabbing and tossing a bowling ball, pulling back and firing a slingshot, and much more.

kid.simple: UI (user interface) is everything players see and click that is not the 3D world itself: health bars, shop menus, buttons, name tags, and more. This page is a map of all the UI tools Roblox gives you. UI can sit flat on the player's screen or live inside the 3D world, like a sign on a wall. Most UI is built from a few basic pieces: frames, labels, buttons, and text boxes.
kid.analogy: Building UI is like making a poster with stickers: frames are the boards, labels are the text and pictures you stick on, and buttons are stickers you can press.
keyPoints: On-screen UI goes in a `ScreenGui` and shows on the player's screen; it lives and runs on the player's device (the client).
In-world UI uses a `SurfaceGui` (stuck to a part's face) or a `BillboardGui` (floats and always faces the camera).
`Frame` holds other UI, `TextLabel`/`ImageLabel` show text or pictures, `TextButton`/`ImageButton` can be clicked, and `TextBox` lets players type.
`Position`, `Size`, `AnchorPoint`, and `ZIndex` control where UI goes, how big it is, and what sits on top.
Tweening smoothly animates UI from one look or spot to another.
Layouts like `UIListLayout` and grids line items up for you, and modifiers like `UIStroke` and `UIGradient` add outlines and color fades.
Universal styling lets you set looks in one place and apply them everywhere, a bit like CSS on websites.
Proximity prompts, UI drag detectors, and 3D drag detectors add ready-made ways for players to interact.

terms.UI / GUI: User interface or graphical user interface. The menus, buttons, and text on top of or inside your game.
terms.GuiObject: Any 2D UI piece you can place, such as a frame, label, button, or text box.
terms.container: An object that holds UI so it can be shown, like `ScreenGui`, `SurfaceGui`, or `BillboardGui`.
terms.client: The player's own device (computer, phone, console). On-screen UI is handled there, not on the server.
terms.AnchorPoint: The spot on a UI object that its `Position` refers to. (0, 0) is the top-left corner; (0.5, 0.5) is the center.
terms.ZIndex: A number that decides which UI is drawn on top. A higher ZIndex covers a lower one.
terms.tweening: Smoothly changing a property over time, like sliding a menu in over 0.5 seconds instead of popping it in.
terms.stylesheet: A list of style rules (colors, fonts, sizes) you write once and apply to lots of UI.

watchOut: On-screen UI is controlled by the client, so change it from a `LocalScript`, not a server `Script`.
Do not cram everything into one big frame. Use frames and layouts to keep UI tidy and easy to move.
Remember players use phones too. Test your UI in different screen sizes.
